findings.text: When lock debugging is active the per CPU guard records its holder on acquisition and its release path warns if the current holder differs from the caller, then clears the holder and forwards to the generic map release using the caller address. Initialization clears the holder. When debugging is inactive the same acquisition, release and initialization names exist as empty operations and the static initializer macros expand to nothing.

Static per CPU guards start from the debug initializer. Dynamic setup allocates a per site class key, validates that no live tracking state overlaps the object, registers the dependency map with LD_WAIT_CONFIG inner, LD_WAIT_INV outer and LD_LOCK_PERCPU category, or with LD_LOCK_NORMAL for nested bottom half spin use, then clears debug ownership, with try setup delegating to plain setup. The common acquisition step marks a try capable guard as taken after asserting it was free and then performs dependency acquisition. Plain, interrupt disabled and interrupt saved variants first suppress preemption or interrupts and then run that step while annotating the context as held.

A try capable per CPU guard is free when its taken marker is clear and held when set. Observation uses a single atomic load on the current CPU instance. A try first suppresses preemption or saves interrupts, returns failure and restores the prior suppression when the marker is already set, otherwise sets the marker and performs dependency acquisition for the try path. Release performs dependency release first and then asserts the marker was set before clearing it.

Unlock drops the held context annotation, runs the common release step and then reenables preemption or interrupts or restores saved interrupt state. Nested bottom half lock and unlock only perform dependency acquisition and release while requiring soft interrupt context, leaving preemption and interrupt masking unchanged.

In the realtime configuration both the plain and try capable per CPU guard types are aliases of the standard spin type. Their static initializers use the unlocked spin initializer and their dynamic initializers forward to the local spin initializer, with the try variant delegating to the plain variant.

Realtime acquisition disables migration before taking the underlying spin lock and release unlocks the spin before reenabling migration. Interrupt disabled and interrupt saved spellings collapse to the same sequence while checking the flag operand type and clearing it. Nested bottom half handling asserts soft interrupt function context and only takes or releases the spin without migration control.

Realtime try fails immediately when called in non maskable or hard interrupt context. Otherwise it disables migration and attempts a spin try lock, reenabling migration on failure. The interrupt saved spelling clears its flag operand and delegates to the plain try. The locked query reports held when the real time owner of the current CPU instance equals the calling task.

Two overloads resolve a per CPU guard base to the calling CPU instance, one for the plain type and one for the try capable type, each promising a held context on return. A macro fallback provides the same resolution without typing.

Copying a dependency map duplicates the whole structure and then clears its class cache array, trading performance to avoid observing torn pointers when another CPU updates the cache concurrently. A dependency node carries entry linkage, class source, links_to target, trace reference, distance count, dep bitmap, only_xr marker and parent search link whose low bit records visitation.
A dependency chain entry packs irq_context in 2 bits, depth in 6 bits and base in 24 bits into one word, followed by padding, hash linkage entry and a 64 bit chain_key.

Recursion accounting reserves 16 low bits for depth, defines the disable bias as 1 shifted by that width and the depth mask as bias minus 1. Held state reports -1 for unknown, 0 for not held and 1 for held. Single depth nesting depth is 1. Forced read recursion and recursive read detection are both always 0. The lock dependency header guard is defined.
Disabling dependency tracking adds the disable bias to the current task recursion counter and enabling subtracts the same bias, so nesting depth in the low bits survives across disabled regions.

Enabled map setup funnels through a common typed initializer with subclass and inner, outer and category arguments, where the narrower helpers supply a normal category and an invalid outer or inner wait kind by default. When tracking is disabled all setup spellings become empty statements that only reference name and key to silence unused warnings.

Enabled class changes re register the guard dependency map while preserving its inner wait, outer wait and lock category and varying only key, symbolic name or subclass, including dedicated keys that disable validation or tracking. Disabled builds replace every spelling with an empty statement that discards its key or name arguments.

Class matching compares the stored key pointer for identity. Held queries extract the dependency map from the guard and delegate to a typed held test with a wildcard reader value, while the disabled held type test always reports held.

Enabled runtime reclassification records the caller address while preserving symbolic name and key and changing validation key or subclass, with one spelling forcing the no validation key. Disabled builds make the setters and the global initializer empty.

The nil pin is a zero valued cookie when enabled and an empty cookie when disabled. A wait override map carries a derived wait override name with a caller supplied inner wait kind and an override lock category when enabled, and an empty possibly unused object when disabled. Pinning returns a cookie from the map and repin and unpin forward map and cookie, while disabled pinning returns an empty cookie and repin and unpin discard their inputs.

Sequence numbers derive from the guard map and depth reads the task held count only while global debug is active, otherwise zero. Enabled assertions warn when debugging is active and the condition fails, with once variants warning at most once, held variants additionally informing static context tracking for exclusive or shared ownership, and a none held check requiring zero depth. Disabled assertions do nothing except that held spellings still inform static tracking. Recursion depth reads the task counter when enabled and zero otherwise.

When tracking is disabled task initialization, recursion toggles, self test binding and the core acquire, release and downgrade operations all exist as empty operations accepting their usual arguments.
Reset reenables global debug. Key range release and exit handling do nothing. Key registration and unregistration accept a class key and do nothing.

The comparator setter forwards guard map plus extra arguments to the map comparator helper when enabled and discards all inputs when disabled. Cross lock context orders XHLOCK_HARD then XHLOCK_SOFT with XHLOCK_CTX_NR as count.
A static map initializer records a symbolic name and a class key pointer. Invariant state enforcement and per task cleanup accept their arguments and do nothing in this configuration.

Enabled contention wrappers first try the fast path and only on failure record contention and take the slow path, then record acquisition, with a returning spelling that propagates the slow path error and records acquisition solely on success. Disabled builds invoke the slow path directly and make contention and acquisition records empty.
Interrupt trace printing accepts a task reference and performs no action in this configuration.

A map copy that retains cached classes risks torn reads under concurrent updates, so the cache must be cleared. The search parent pointer carries a visited mark in its low bit and must be masked before use as an address.

Realtime try in non maskable or hard interrupt context must report failure without altering migration or lock state, and any failed spin try after disabling migration must reenable migration to keep the pairing balanced.
